summary: The change meets the acceptance criteria: cl_http_utility=>decode_base64 compiles and runs under osgo (verified end-to-end for the alias and if_http_utility~ call syntaxes, padded/unpadded/URL-safe base64, U+FFFD replacement and strlen over multibyte results), and nodeutf8.Decode matched Node's Buffer.from(bytes).toString() on ~424k differential cases including exhaustive interesting-byte combinations. The full pipeline also matched Node on 80k adversarial base64 strings (embedded '=', whitespace, junk, odd lengths); the only divergence found is for non-ASCII characters inside the base64 text, inherited from the pre-existing DecodeXBase64. Remaining findings are minor: that non-ASCII divergence, one dead NATIVE entry, and a gofmt nit in the new test file.

findings.claim: DecodeBase64 diverges from Node's Buffer.from(encoded, "base64") when `encoded` contains non-ASCII characters: Node converts the string to latin1 before base64-decoding, so a character whose low byte is an alphabet symbol is decoded (U+0141 'Ł' -> 0x41 'A', U+013D 'Ľ' -> 0x3D '='), while the reused DecodeXBase64 skips the character's UTF-8 bytes (and never stops at such a padding byte). The task requires text consistent with Node and Node's handling of extraneous characters; this is a real, reproducible deviation, though it is confined to non-ASCII base64 input and is inherited from the pre-existing, already-shipped DecodeXBase64 used by decode_x_base64 (all ASCII inputs match Node exactly in an 80k-case differential fuzz).
findings.repro: input 'QŁJD' (Q,U+0141,J,D): node -e 'process.stdout.write(Buffer.from("Q\u0141JD","base64").toString("hex"))' prints 400243; abap.DecodeBase64(nil, "QŁJD") returns 40efbfbd. Likewise 'QUĽJD': Node 41 (stops at Ľ->'='), Go 414243.

findings.claim: The NATIVE entry ["CL_HTTP_UTILITY=>DECODE_BASE64", "abap.DecodeBase64"] is dead code: NATIVE keys are `${className}=>${name}` with the method name as written in the class implementation, and cl_http_utility implements the method only as 'METHOD if_http_utility~decode_base64' (ALIASES do not produce MethodDef entries, and redefinedAlias maps redefinitions back to the '~' name), so only the IF_HTTP_UTILITY~DECODE_BASE64 entry at line 738 can fire. Harmless (if it ever fired the emitted call would be identical), but inconsistent with encode_base64, which registers only the interface-method key.
findings.repro: grep -n '^  METHOD' .local/pins/open-abap-core*/src/http/cl_http_utility.clas.abap  # no 'METHOD decode_base64.' exists, only if_http_utility~decode_base64

findings.claim: The new test file is not gofmt-clean: the trailing comments in the case table are mis-aligned (gofmt wants the comment columns equalized across rows 16-18). No repo gate enforces gofmt and several pre-existing files also deviate, so this is cosmetic.
